thread:
sam: Quick favor — can someone run a warmup baseline on vpc-dev-17? After the private deploy last night we're seeing CPU stalls and token p95 regressions on cold starts. Need a short run with the latest model pinned + flamegraph capture.
jess: On it. Do you want the usual `warmup.sh` + `capture-flame.sh` combo, or a lighter quick-check?
sam: Start with quick-check: 100 requests, seq_len=512, model=redwood-v2.3-pin. Capture `top`/`perf record` for the p95 spike windows. If it's noisy I'll escalate to full warmup.
mike: I can run now — which host exactly? vpc-dev-17 or the control group too?
sam: vpc-dev-17 first, then run the same on hosted-staging-3 for parity. Put results in /tmp/warmup-runs/<yourname>-205500.
mike: Running `ssh infra@vpc-dev-17 'cd /opt/bench && ./quick-warmup --count 100 --seq 512 --model redwood-v2.3-pin'`. Posting logs when done.
infra-bot: CI triggered: infra/warmup-checks on vpc-dev-17 #205500 (logs: https://ci.internal/runs/205500/).
leo: If you see p95 spikes check `fsync` and pagecache churn — on baremetal we had issues when `swapiness` was default. Also compare /proc/interrupts before/after.
anita: Also confirm hugepages and transparent hugepages state. On some onprem images THP caused stally behavior for mmap-heavy workloads. Run `cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` and `grep Huge /proc/meminfo` before warmup.
mike: Quick results: p95 went from 48ms (hosted) to 210ms (vpc-dev-17). Attached short log snippet: ```
[2025-05-12T10:12:34Z] req=87 p95=210ms cpu%usr=72.3 cpu%sys=18.4 iowait=4.1
[2025-05-12T10:12:58Z] req=100 p95=198ms cpu%usr=68.1 cpu%sys=20.2 iowait=6.0
```
sam: Yikes. Can you re-run with KV cache disabled (env NO_KV_CACHE=1) and with cpufreq governor set to performance? Might isolate freq-capping vs cache correctness.
mike: Re-run queued. Also grabbing `perf record -F 99 -a -g` during the next 100 requests and will push `perf.data` to the run dir.
runtime-ci: Warmup run finished. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/205500/warmup-mike.tar.gz (flamegraph.html, perf.data, logs).
jess: Thanks — I'll diff the flamegraph against hosted-staging-3 and look for syscalls vs user hotspots. If I find heavy `futex` or `epoll_wait` we might be hitting cgroups/io throttle.
anita: If futex shows up, also check kernel version and `CONFIG_PREEMPT` differences. On one customer box a different preempt config changed scheduling latency.
sam: Great. After jess does the diff, can we triage in async thread and decide next steps? If it's infra-config we open a private runbook item. If it's model-runtime, we'll roll a canary with `NO_KV_CACHE` baseline and quantify delta. :thumbsup:
